clue.text: Alcoholic haze?

parts.note: a fine drizzly fog named after Scotland, read as if it were a vapour of whisky

explanation.surface: A boozy blur, the fog in a drinker's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is the Scottish name for a thick drizzly mist; the question mark flags the pun reading Scotch as whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The name pairs Scotch, a whisky, with mist, a haze, so a whimsical whisky fog fits.

clue.text: Rob has to leave work

definitions.meaning: slang for stealing, as in thieves who nick goods
to finish for the day and go home

explanation.surface: A worker who must quit the job to turn thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal phrasal-verb senses: steal from someone, and stop working for the day.

clue.text: Sunseekers take off for this state

definitions.text: Sunseekers take off for this state

parts.words: Sunseekers take off for this state
parts.note: sunbathers who strip off everything reach a condition of being unclothed, while 'take off for' suggests flying away to a destination

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers flying off to some sunny country or US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off for this state' reads as flying to a place; really it is removing clothes to reach a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely unclothed is a condition, the state sunbathers reach by stripping.

clue.text: It may be used to lift a football side

definitions.text: It may be used to lift
definitions.meaning: an aerofoil on an aircraft gives it lift
the flank of the pitch, or the player stationed out there

explanation.surface: Something used to hoist a football team, as if a crane lifted the side.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeroplane's aerofoil generates lift, and the touchline flank of a football pitch is also so called.

clue.text: Crashing gears gives feeling full of hostility

indicators.note: crashing gears grind and jumble, so these two words' letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver grinding the gearbox, getting angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crashing' rearranges the letters of GEARS and GIVES together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hostile is combative and ready to attack, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Face up? It might mean the opposite!

definitions.text: Face up? It might mean the opposite!

parts.words: Face up? It might mean the opposite!
parts.note: to confront something is to face up to it; retreating from a position is its opposite, and back is literally opposite face and down opposite up

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether something lies face up or the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word is the opposite of its partner: back against face, down against up, and the phrase means to retreat rather than confront.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat from a stance is the reverse of confronting it, and the words mirror the clue's pair.

clue.text: Colin goes out East to see her

indicators.note: going out of shape, the boy's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: Colin steps out eastward to visit a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' is a bare pronoun standing for any woman, here one bearing this name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's given name, so a woman can be referred to by it.

clue.text: Expert in Polish

definitions.meaning: an enthusiast who knows a lot, as in a film fan
to rub something until it shines

explanation.surface: Someone skilled in the Polish language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is the verb to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: An enthusiast with deep knowledge, and to shine by rubbing, are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Blaming a number before making sure

indicators.note: the numeral is placed ahead of the next piece

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone who checks the figures carefully before blaming anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Formally criticising someone strongly is a form of blaming or condemning them.

clue.text: A valediction is something cast in gold

indicators.note: the cast item sits inside the symbol for the precious metal

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is cast, thrown in a game of dice

explanation.surface: A farewell speech immortalised as a gilded statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something cast' is not a metal casting but a die, rolled at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the French farewell, used in English to bid someone goodbye, a parting word.

clue.text: Taking another course in sewing

definitions.meaning: a sailing boat changing direction against the wind
making long loose stitches to hold fabric temporarily

explanation.surface: A student switching to a needlework class.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors zigzag upwind by changing heading, and tailors use loose temporary stitches; one word covers both.

clue.text: A roué not waiting for his cut?

parts.note: a roué is a dissolute pleasure-seeker, a rake
someone off has already left, so is not waiting around

explanation.surface: A womaniser leaving without waiting for his share.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an illicit share of profits, someone's percentage or slice.

clue.text: It's played when one is out of form

definitions.text: It's played when one is out of form

parts.words: It's played when one is out of form
parts.note: a form is a school class; a pupil skipping lessons plays truant, also said with this word, while 'out of form' suggests a slumping athlete

explanation.surface: Something a sportsman plays while going through a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class, so being out of form here means absent from lessons; truanting is to 'play' this, chiefly in American use.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipping school without permission is called playing truant, or playing this.

clue.text: Untruthful hedonists booted out

indicators.note: kicked out of place, the pleasure-seekers' letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lying pleasure-seekers thrown out of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booted out' rearranges the letters of HEDONISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A lying person is deceitful, lacking honesty: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Means to secure artistic work?

parts.note: a tack for fixing sheets to a board, read as an artist's sketch plus a fastener

explanation.surface: Some way of obtaining a commission for art, like a grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secure' looks like obtaining; it is fastening, and 'artistic work' is the sketch being pinned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-headed tack holds paper to a board, such as an artist's sketch.

clue.text: Straddles and makes a capture at sea in skirmish

parts.note: to capture a piece in chess is to take it

indicators.note: a skirmish is a scuffle, so the words are jumbled about

explanation.surface: A naval battle in which one ship sits astride and seizes another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in skirmish' rearranges AT SEA into A SEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Straddling a chair or a horse is a way of sitting down on it.

clue.text: Where to obtain counter-intelligence?

parts.note: intelligence across a counter: an enquiry point where staff hand out facts, rather than espionage work

explanation.surface: A spy asking where to get anti-espionage secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter-intelligence' looks like spycraft; it is information given over a counter.
explanation.definitionFit: An enquiry point in a station or store hands out facts over a counter.

clue.text: Cracked clues once more, being determined

definitions.meaning: having worked out the puzzles again, solved a second time
firm in intention, having made up one's mind

explanation.surface: A dogged solver going over the clues again.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as RE-SOLVED, solved again.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone firmly decided is resolute; read as re-solved, the puzzles were cracked again.

clue.text: Put ban on spirits and remove without alternative

indicators.note: without means outside, so the cutting word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: to excise is to cut out or remove
OR is the word that offers an alternative

explanation.surface: A prohibitionist banning liquor and removing it entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests alcohol; they are ghosts or demons, and 'without' here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving out an evil spirit by ritual is a way of banishing ghosts.

clue.text: Turn out when a sprinter is replaced

indicators.note: put back in a different place, the runner's letters take a new order

explanation.surface: An athlete is substituted, and we see how things go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is replaced' rearranges the letters of A SPRINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: When something comes to light or happens, it is said to emerge or prove so.

clue.text: It is weighed by craftsmen

parts.note: craft are boats, so craftsmen are sailors, who weigh (raise) the mooring weight before leaving port

explanation.surface: Artisans putting something on the scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftsmen' suggests artisans; it means men of the boats, and to weigh it is to haul it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors raise the heavy hooked weight that holds a ship, which is called weighing it.

clue.text: Sweets for kids

definitions.meaning: desserts of puréed fruit with cream, such as gooseberry
to kid someone is to trick or tease them

explanation.surface: Treats bought for the children.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of fruit folded into cream; 'kids' is a verb, not children.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit-and-cream puddings carry this name, and to hoodwink someone is the same word.

clue.text: Sacking and burning

definitions.meaning: baking pottery in a kiln, or setting alight

explanation.surface: Looting and setting fire, as in a sacked city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacking' suggests plundering a town; it is dismissal from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissal from employment and the heating of clay in a kiln share this word.

clue.text: Finance record reveals arrears

parts.note: to back a venture is to finance it
a log is a written record, as a ship keeps

explanation.surface: An account ledger exposing unpaid debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Work or payments piled up and still outstanding form an accumulation of arrears.

clue.text: Support a play or a player

definitions.meaning: to put money behind a theatre production
a defender in football or rugby

explanation.surface: Deciding whether to sponsor a show or one actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests an actor; it is a defensive team player.
explanation.definitionFit: Investors fund a show by backing it, and a defender in team sports holds this position.

clue.text: Mascara make-up used by Latin American entertainers

indicators.note: made up anew, the cosmetic's letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Eye cosmetics worn by Latin American performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like the cosmetics theme; it rearranges the letters of MASCARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumba bands shake these gourd rattles, instruments that Latin American musicians play.

clue.text: Put under pressure to serve up the cheese

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Edam is the round Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: A waiter pressured into bringing out the cheese course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve up' reverses EDAM in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being forced or compelled to do something is to have been coerced, a sense of the past tense.

clue.text: Stop being stuffy

definitions.meaning: to shut or bring to an end
muggy and airless, as weather can be

explanation.surface: No longer acting pompous or prim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffy' suggests stuck-up; it is airless and humid.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut or end, and muggy airless weather, share one spelling with different pronunciations.

clue.text: Is done in a different way in the Far East

indicators.note: put together a different way, these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Things are done otherwise out in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different way' rearranges IS DONE IN A; the definition is loose, the country being part of the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: The island republic lies in South-East Asia, one of the countries of the Far East.
